name: Light and Heavy Chain Deposition Disease
aliases: Light and Heavy Chain Deposition Disease (LHCDD)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Light and Heavy Chain Deposition Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Demonstration of non-amyloid monoclonal light and heavy chain deposits in kidney biopsy by immunofluorescence and electron microscopy
Presence of monoclonal gammopathy or plasma cell dyscrasia confirmed by serum or urine immunofixation electrophoresis
Clinical evidence of renal impairment such as proteinuria, hematuria, or reduced glomerular filtration rate
Exclusion of amyloidosis by Congo red staining negativity and absence of fibrillar deposits on electron microscopy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (histopathological confirmation of deposits, monoclonal gammopathy, and renal dysfunction) must be met with exclusion of amyloidosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires kidney biopsy with immunofluorescence and electron microscopy to differentiate from other monoclonal immunoglobulin deposition diseases.

laboratory: Monoclonal immunoglobulin light and heavy chains detected by serum and urine immunofixation electrophoresis
Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen indicating renal impairment
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal or increased echogenicity
Skeletal survey may reveal lytic lesions if associated plasma cell dyscrasia present
Echocardiogram may show restrictive cardiomyopathy in rare cardiac involvement
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; disease associated with clonal plasma cell disorders
other: Kidney biopsy with immunofluorescence demonstrating linear deposits of monoclonal light and heavy chains along basement membranes
Electron microscopy showing granular electron-dense deposits without fibrillar structure

distinguishingFeatures: Only light chain deposits without heavy chain involvement
Similar renal manifestations but absence of heavy chain deposits on biopsy
Presence of Congo red positive fibrillar deposits
May involve light chains, heavy chains, or both but requires differentiation by biopsy
Clinical presentation overlaps but requires immunofluorescence for precise typing

redFlags: Evidence of systemic plasma cell dyscrasia
